exposure: new-onset acute myeloid leukemia (AML) during pregnancy
timing of AML diagnosis during pregnancy
outcome: pregnancy outcomes (therapeutic abortion, preterm/full-term birth, maternal survival, maternal remission)
neonatal outcomes (live birth, congenital malformations, NICU admission, newborn complete blood counts and biochemical examinations)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 25 pregnant women diagnosed with new-onset acute myeloid leukemia (AML) during their pregnancy between January 2010 and January 2021.
finding: New-onset AML diagnosed in an earlier stage of pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of poor pregnancy outcomes, while neonatal outcomes for those receiving proper treatment are generally good.
gest_age: The study included 9 preterm and 4 full-term newborns, but specific birth gestational ages for the entire cohort are not provided; gestational age at AML diagnosis ranged from 16.9 ± 4.4 weeks to 29.7 ± 5.5 weeks.
